keyTakeaways.headline: Flood disruption widens into a fourth day - Shah Alam hotspots flooded again and forecasts cover Pahang and Kelantan until Wednesday
keyTakeaways.soWhat: Brace for stop-work and logistics delays spreading east; Lee Lam Thye's drainage-overhaul call adds political pressure for stricter drainage compliance on active KL sites.

keyTakeaways.headline: AI labs are now buying power-generation equipment outright - Anthropic's US$3.4b generator deal is the largest single purchase yet (FT)
keyTakeaways.soWhat: Power access is replacing chips as the buildout bottleneck; Malaysian DC economics compete in the same global queue for turbines and generators.

sectors.theme: Flood risk widens toward the east coast as KL's drainage comes under fire

items.headline: Flood risk widens: Taman Sri Muda floods again, forecasts warn Pahang and Kelantan districts until Wednesday
items.detail: Flash floods hit Taman Sri Muda and Kampung Baru Hicom in Shah Alam on Sunday afternoon after heavy rain, with water spilling onto roads from overflowing drains but no evacuations, the Selangor Fire and Rescue Department said. Forecasts now warn of flooding in Kuantan, Pekan and Rompin in Pahang and nine districts in Kelantan until Wednesday, while the Alliance for a Safe Community's Lee Lam Thye called for a comprehensive overhaul of Kuala Lumpur's drainage and flood mitigation systems, citing clogged drains, silt and irresponsible construction activity. The warnings follow three days of evacuations across Selangor, Perak and Penang and Selangor's halt on Puncak Alam development works.
items.soWhat: The disruption window now extends to mid-week on the east coast while the Klang Valley keeps flooding on single-hour downpours - site access, materials logistics and drainage-compliance scrutiny on active projects all tighten.

sectors.theme: Anthropic's US$3.4b generator deal shows power access is the new AI bottleneck

items.headline: Anthropic agrees to pay US$3.4b for gas-fired generators to power AI data centres - FT
items.detail: Anthropic PBC agreed to pay US$3.4 billion for gas-fired generators for data centres in what the Financial Times described as the largest known single purchase of power-generation equipment by an AI lab, the newspaper reported. The company bought commitments for 1.7 gigawatts of heavy-duty generators from San Antonio-based OnePWR Solutions in late September, taking over its Caterpillar Inc generator orders rather than buying power from the supplier. Anthropic has said it intends to spend more than US$895 billion in the years ahead, mostly on computing power and infrastructure.
items.soWhat: AI labs are bypassing utilities and buying generation equipment outright - power access, not chips, is becoming the binding constraint on data-centre buildouts, which sets the economics for every DC market competing for the same equipment, Malaysia included. (Foreign item; FT report carried by The Edge.)
